cards.title: Control Only What Is Within You
cards.insight: Stoicism teaches that external events—market crashes, job losses, criticism—lie beyond our command. What remains eternally yours is your judgment, effort, and response. The Stoic practitioner accepts circumstances while directing full agency toward reasoned choices and virtue.
cards.takeaway: When facing an uncontrollable situation, ask: 'What is my responsibility here?' and act with integrity on that answer.

cards.title: Perspective Through Scaled Time
cards.insight: A setback that feels catastrophic today shrinks in significance when viewed across a lifetime or human history. Stoics practiced premeditatio malorum—imagining worst-case scenarios—not to paralyze, but to reduce the shock and clarify what genuinely matters. This temporal reframing dissolves false urgencies.
cards.takeaway: When stressed, step back: How important will this feel in five years? Let that perspective guide your effort.

cards.title: Virtue as the Sole True Good
cards.insight: Stoicism breaks ties with popular culture's obsession with wealth, status, and comfort. Instead, it posits that only living with wisdom, justice, courage, and temperance constitutes genuine success. External gains pale against the inner alignment required by virtue.
cards.takeaway: Measure your day's success by your character and effort, not by outcomes or possessions.

cards.title: The Power of Acceptance
cards.insight: Stoics do not passively surrender to injustice; rather, they accept reality as it is—not as they wish it were—so they can act effectively within it. Resistance to facts wastes energy; acceptance clarifies where action can take root.
cards.takeaway: State the facts plainly, grieve if needed, then ask: 'Given reality as it is, what is my next move?'
